podcast.title: Blink-182's Departure (2012)
podcast.body: Blink-182 formally split from Interscope Records in October 2012. This decision allowed the band to release music independently, providing them with complete creative freedom and eliminating external interference in their projects. "They left Interscope Records in October 2012."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Audioslave Co-Release (First Album) – Partnership with Epic
podcast.body: Interscope Records, Chris Cornell's label, collaborated with Epic Records (Rage Against the Machine's label) for the joint release of Audioslave's debut album. This was part of a negotiated deal to navigate the band members' existing contractual obligations. "The first album would be released by both Epic, Rage Against the Machine's label, and Interscope, Chris's label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Audioslave Release (Third Album for US) – Continued Involvement
podcast.body: Interscope Records managed the US release of Audioslave's third album, while Epic handled the international release. This arrangement concluded the complex label deal that had been negotiated for the supergroup's releases. "then the third album would be Interscope for the US and Epic for the rest of the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Audioslave Sole Release (Second Album) – Exclusive Distribution
podcast.body: Interscope Records held exclusive distribution rights for Audioslave's second album, as part of the label compromise worked out during the band's formation. This followed a joint release for their debut and preceded a split arrangement for their third. "The second album would be Interscope only..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fred Durst as Executive
podcast.body: Fred Durst, known for his role in Limp Bizkit, later became a major executive at Interscope Records, demonstrating a unique career trajectory from artist to industry leader. "Fred has since become a major executive at Interscope Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 3

podcast.title: Jimmy Iovine's Influence
podcast.body: Jimmy Iovine is recognized as a skilled marketer and played a supportive role in Bush's recordings. He also co-founded Beats with Dr. Dre, driven partly by concerns over the poor quality of available headphones. "Which in the Iveane, that took a care of quite a bit of it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bush: The Post-CD Band  Featuring Gavin Rossdale

podcast.title: Rescue of Trent Reznor
podcast.body: Producer Jimmy Iovine brought Trent Reznor into the fold of Interscope Records after his "suffocating deal" with TVT Records was resolved, allowing Trent to record his second album without further dispute. "After Trent was rescued from the suffocating deal with TVT records producer Jimmy Iovine brought him into the fold of interscope records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rescuing Nine Inch Nails from TVT
podcast.body: Interscope Records played a crucial role in liberating Nine Inch Nails from their restrictive and litigious contract with TVT Records. Trent Reznor initially viewed the move as "the lesser of several evils" due to his perception of Interscope's image at the time (e.g., Marky Mark), but later appreciated having a label president who, as a former producer, understood the challenges of making records. "They rescued us from TBT, it was a lesser of several evils, and at the time my vision of the inner scope was Mark E. Mark, it was like, Christ, one TVT, and another."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Deep Dark Secrets of Nine Inch Nails

podcast.title: Support for Artists
podcast.body: Interscope Records, particularly with Jimmy Iovine, provided substantial financial, emotional, and musical backing to Bush over the years. Gavin Rossdale began recording his "Sea of Memories" album while still under Interscope's care. "I had the benefit, the backing and the financial support, emotional support, musical support of the team at Indusco that always helped me greatly over the years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
